symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1252: a Studio Pro 11.12.3 Aggregate list activity with a custom error handler (with or without rollback) described as a bare `$count = count($TEYAs);`, and `on error` was a parse error (mismatched input 'on' expecting ';') on list operations, aggregates, create list, add/remove, cast, rollback and show home page. MDL077 additionally refused the clause on list operations and aggregates.
cause: THREE LAYERS, one false premise. (1) Grammar: eight statement rules had no onErrorClause. (2) MDL077 asserted Microflows$ListOperationsAction and AggregateAction have no ErrorHandlingType 'in the metamodel' — the Model SDK declares it on the base Microflows$MicroflowAction, which every one of them extends, with an unbounded StructureVersionInfo; the vendored gen types and the #591 writers carried it too. (3) Reader: actionFromGen never read ErrorHandlingType off RollbackAction or ShowHomePageAction (and their sdk structs had no field), so DESCRIBE's gate saw "" and dropped the whole handler branch. The list activities DID read it, so on HEAD their describe emitted a live clause the grammar then refused — the #1078 trap again.
fix: onErrorClause on the eight rules; AST fields; builders use ehType(clause) + finishCustomErrorHandler (rollback/home page use explicitErrorHandling so no-clause BSON is unchanged); add/remove to a reference set pass the clause to the Change object activity; MDL077 (error-handling) removed; MDL076 and the nanoflow without-rollback-only rule extended from a measured matrix; reader/writer carry the type on rollback and show home page.
insight: **Settle 'not in the metamodel' against the Model SDK before writing a rule on it.** MDL077's premise took one grep to refute: `npm pack mendixmodelsdk`, then errorHandlingType sits on the base MicroflowAction class every action extends — a property on a base class is invisible to a per-type search. A refusal rule built on an unverified absence turns a capability gap into an enforced one. **Measure, do not extrapolate, the accepted forms**: one 11.12.3 project with one microflow AND one nanoflow per (statement x clause) cell — 85 documents, a single `mx check -j out.json` (the JSON names the document; the text output does not) — gave the whole matrix in one build. It is not guessable: in a microflow all eight take custom handlers and reject continue EXCEPT rollback, which takes continue; in a nanoflow the list activities and cast share create/commit's 'without rollback only' row while rollback takes everything; show home page is microflow-only. **Default-preservation is per writer**: rollback's writer never stored a type and show home page's always stored a literal Rollback, so both use explicitErrorHandling; the list activities already wrote ehType(nil) and keep ehType. Controls: stub the visitor assignment -> builder test reports 0 Custom activities; drop the reader line -> ErrorHandlingType ""; drop the MDL076 rows -> continue accepted. describe -> exec of the matrix reports every document already in sync.
